stories.teaser: GPS trackers now watch over half of Israel’s vultures
stories.headline: GPS trackers help Israel protect its vultures, with half the population now tagged
stories.why: Just over 100 vultures carry transmitters; about 60 more will be tagged this fall, aiming for 75%.
texts:
Every vulture in the sky over Israel matters.

The Israel Nature and Parks Authority just released two vultures in the Lower Galilee with new GPS transmitters. One flew toward Mount Carmel, the other to Gamla Nature Reserve. Just over 100 vultures, nearly half of Israel’s population, now carry trackers that help protect them.

“The transmitters are our eyes in the field,” says ecologist Dr. Ohad Hatzofe.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife

100+ vultures tracked. 60 more this fall. Goal: 75% of the population.

The Israel Nature and Parks Authority, working with Tel Aviv University researchers, is fitting Israel’s vultures with GPS transmitters so it can follow them and protect them from threats like poisoning. Two freshly tagged vultures were just released in the Lower Galilee.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife

How do you protect a bird that can fly across the whole country in a day?

You give it a GPS tracker. Nearly half of Israel’s vultures now carry one, and about 60 more will be tagged this fall with help from Tel Aviv University.

“The transmitters are our eyes in the field. Without them, we are blind,” says Dr. Ohad Hatzofe of the Israel Nature and Parks Authority.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife
stories.og_title: GPS trackers reveal where vultures fly after release in Israel

stories.teaser: A 25-ton, 2,000-year-old ritual bath moved in one piece
stories.headline: Israel moves a 2,000-year-old, 25-ton ritual bath in one piece
stories.why: Found in Kiryat Gat, the mikveh is evidence of the first Jewish settlement known in the area.
texts:
Imagine lifting 2,000 years of history with a crane, and not letting it crack.

Israel Antiquities Authority conservators spent two weeks reinforcing a Second Temple-era mikveh found in Kiryat Gat, then lifted all 25 tons with a 300-ton crane. When building in the neighborhood is done, it’s expected to return for public display.

“Once you lift a structure like this, there is no going back,” says senior conservator Eyal Kahu.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage

25 tons. About 4 meters across. Around 2,000 years old.

The Israel Antiquities Authority moved a Second Temple-era ritual bath from Kiryat Gat in one piece, using steel beams, protective wrapping and a 300-ton crane. Excavation directors say it belongs to the first Jewish settlement known in that area. It is planned to go back on public display in the neighborhood.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage

How do you move a 2,000-year-old room?

Very carefully. Israel Antiquities Authority teams braced a 25-ton ritual bath from Kiryat Gat with steel beams and foam, then lifted it whole.

“The day before an operation like this, you don’t sleep,” says conservator Eyal Kahu. “You’re under pressure because the responsibility is yours and there is no room for mistakes.”

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage
stories.og_title: Israel moves 2,000-year-old mikveh intact in complex 25-ton operation
